correctness.rationale: The universal inequality is reduced to four vertex checks because all relevant line-distance sums are affine on the convex quadrilateral. At each vertex, exact circle geometry gives a normalized defect E=x^2+y^2+z^2-sqrt(2)y(x+z), and 2E=(x-z)^2+(x+z-sqrt(2)y)^2. Equality at an interior point forces every vertex defect to vanish, which cyclically forces all four half-arc gaps to equal pi/4. The square converse is direct. No finite experiment is used as the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2016 primary conjecture explicitly asks for the general cyclic-polygon extension and identifies only the triangle case as proved; its current public page contains no answer. Exact-statement and implication searches found no n=4 tangent-line theorem. The most relevant later full text inspected, arXiv:2105.07885, remains triangle-only. Classical and weighted polygon Erdős–Mordell results use vertex or angle-bisector distances rather than distances to the circumcircle tangents, so they do not imply the claim. Residual risk remains for unindexed literature and inaccessible full text of the 2016 Forum Geometricorum article.
residual_risks: The Forum Geometricorum 2016 PDF was not directly retrievable during this review, though the source conjecture and later full-text literature specify its triangle scope.
The 2005 weighted polygon article was not read in full; available statement-level evidence shows a different vertex/side-distance implication.
Unindexed, non-English, or differently phrased literature could contain the n=4 result despite the searches performed.

value.rationale: The result settles the complete n=4 case of a published 2016 all-n cyclic/tangential polygon conjecture, the first polygonal case beyond the known triangle case. It gives the conjectured sharp coefficient and a full interior equality classification, so it is a natural structural step rather than an arbitrary slice or numerical instance.
